SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: The first multiple regression analysis including the O-LIFE dimensions as potential predictors of the CAQ score revealed a significant effect only in the case of Unusual Experiences, β = 0.23, t(106) = 2.31, p = .05. In the second analysis, LI was added to the O-LIFE dimensions. The effect of Unusual Experience failed to retain significance, β = 0.15, t(105) = 1.64, p = .10. In the third analysis, IQ was added to the above-described model. Its effect was significant, β = 0.27, t(104) = 2.98, p = .05. In the fourth analysis, the size of the primary and secondary group was entered into the regression model. The predictive effect of the primary group was highly significant, β = 0.42, t(103) = 4.98, p = .0001. Finally, we conducted a regression analysis in which we tested the predictors of social network size. As expected from the above reported analyses, in the case of the primary group the single significant predictor was the CAQ score, β = 0.50, t(103) = 5.18, p = .0001. The degrees of freedom for the t-tests (e.g., t(106), t(105), t(104), t(103)) consistently indicate a sample size of N=107 for the regression analyses involving CAQ and IQ (N = df + 1).
